title: discarded traffic signs fold into urban tables for farmers’ markets in new york city
summary:
JUAN FERNÁNDEZ GONZÁLEZ FOLDS TRAFFIC SIGNS INTO URBAN TABLESConceived by architect Juan Fernández González, Traffic Sign Urban Tables is an urban furniture project that repurposes decommissioned aluminum traffic signs into standing tables mounted onto existing street signposts in New York City.
With over one million traffic signs across the five boroughs regularly removed due to graffiti, wear, or legibility loss, the project intercepts municipal waste streams to provide compact dining surfaces for farmers’ markets and mobile food vendors, which typically operate without seating or surface amenities.
The designer hand-paints the tables in a pink-and-white checkered motif referencing traditional disposable street-food tablecloths.
Installation relies entirely on pre-existing U-channel signposts—a Federal Highway Administration standard featuring pre-punched mounting holes spaced one inch center-to-center.
Secured with standard bolts, nuts, and washers, the lightweight units can be height-adjusted, mounted without obstructing pedestrian circulation, and deployed temporarily during street closures.

title: Schools discuss climate change at Dorset Youth COP meeting
summary:
Hosted at the Kingston Maurwood campus, the first Dorset-wide Youth COP has brought children from 14 schools together to discuss issues including future careers.
Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said young people should be "given a voice" over dealing with climate change.
A Dorset COP 2026 event is also being held on Saturday as world leaders and delegates gather at Antalya in Turkey for the COP31 climate summit.
The Dorset Youth COP event includes discussions about how young people feel about climate change as well as a panel session introducing them to the range of jobs and careers in the climate and energy sectors.
"The Youth COP aims to raise awareness, inspire and support them to take action now and into the future."

title: Bluetongue virus confirmed on County Down farm
summary:
The first case of Bluetongue in Northern Ireland this season has been confirmed on a farm in Kilkeel, County Down.
Officials from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera) said the virus had been detected in three sheep.
There will be no additional movement restrictions or disease control zones, because the virus has been present in Northern Ireland since November 2025.
The minister, Andrew Muir, said the discovery of the virus was "disappointing but not unexpected", given the spread of the disease in Great Britain and Ireland.
The Chief Veterinary Officer, Brian Dooher, urged local farmers to be alert to any symptoms in their livestock.

title: US test reactor cleared for operations
summary:
Oklo's Groves Isotope Test Reactor has been cleared for unrestricted operations by the US Department of Energy.
The test reactor, near Lockhart in Caldwell County, Texas reached first criticality in August, less than a year after groundbreaking.
It is one of 11 advanced reactor projects selected by the US Department of Energy (DOE) in August 2025 for the Nuclear Reactor Pilot Program, a programme aiming to expedite the testing of advanced reactor designs under a DOE authorisation pathway.
With Groves-1 now cleared for unrestricted operations, Oklo said it will test its capabilities relevant to future isotope reactors and the company's fast fission reactor, the Aurora powerhouse.
"Now we're building on that experience by operating the reactor, testing new capabilities, and learning directly from the work.

title: Expansion proposal for Brooklyn plants fuels data center fears
summary:
The owner of a pair of floating power plants near Sunset Park, Brooklyn wants to expand the facilities, prompting protests from environmentalists who fear they could be used one day to power data centers.
The Gowanus Generation Station and nearby Narrows Generation Station are peaker facilities that are only activated during periods of peak demand.
The owner of the plants, AlphaGen, submitted an expansion plan to Con Edison earlier this year, stating that it expects the company's operating permit will be extended past 2029.
“Sunset Park is not a dumping ground for dangerous energy projects,” said State Senator Andrew Gounardes, who joined a protest Thursday over the expansion plans.
We demand investments that move us forward and we won’t stop fighting until we get them.”AlphaGen’s expansion proposal “recognizes the realities of current power technology and the need to balance reliability with sustainability,” Curt Morgan, CEO of AlphaGen said in a press release.

title: Countries Growing More Ambitious on Climate, Despite U.S. Retreat
summary:
The Trump administration has moved to dismantle U.S. climate policy, slashing subsidies for clean energy, weakening limits on pollution, and attacking the legal basis for climate regulation.
But the U.S. retreat on climate policy belies advances in Asia, Africa, and Latin America, experts say.
Analyzing climate laws and regulations in 39 countries that account for the bulk of global emissions, researchers at Oxford University find little evidence of a widespread policy retrenchment.
Of those repeals, eight come from the U.S.At the U.N. climate conference now underway in Turkey, “geopolitical divisions risk dominating the headlines,” said Thom Wetzer, codirector of the Oxford Climate Policy Hub, which undertook the research.
In the U.S., Democratic wins in the recent midterm elections have also opened a path for climate progress at the state level, according to Michael Gerrard, director of the Sabin Center for Climate Change Law at Columbia Law School.

title: Indigenous leaders at COP31 say it’s past time to turn promises into action
summary:
“It is still a struggle,” said Edward Porokwa, who is Maasai and a member of the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues.
Porokwa said that he feels that responsibility to address climate change continues to fall on smaller countries and Indigenous peoples.
“For over 30 years we have brought Indigenous knowledges and sciences to these negotiations,” Māori activist Quack Pirihi said in an opening statement on behalf of the International Indigenous Peoples Forum on Climate Change.
But the process to receive and administer those funds is ongoing, and Indigenous leaders say the fund must work faster.
As negotiations continue through November 20, Indigenous advocates will continue their push for all the discussions to lead to tangible actions.

title: Mexico’s Parque del Jaguar protects jaguars with 18-kilometre limestone wall
summary:
Mexican studio Colectivo C733 has created an 18-kilometre-long limestone wall that allows wildlife to pass through while protecting more than 1,000 hectares of forest at Parque del Jaguar in Tulum, Mexico.
The park occupies a coastal territory containing tropical forest, mangroves, underground rivers and karstic geology, as well as the ancient Mayan archaeological site of Tulum.
At its perimeter, the studio added an 18-kilometre dry-stacked limestone wall, known locally as a tecorral, informed by traditional Mayan stone boundaries.
“By designing how the territory is revealed, inhabited, and understood over time, Parque del Jaguar shifts architecture from a static intervention to an evolving framework that connects environment, culture, and collective awareness,” Colectivo C733 said.
Founded in 2019, Colectivo C733 brings together the practices of Gabriela Carrillo, Carlos Facio, José Amozurrutia, Eric Valdez and Israel Espín to work on public architecture and urban infrastructure across Mexico.

title: Floods Force Gaza to Choose Between Clean Water and Pumping Out Sewage
summary:
She lives in a shelter in Al Maghazi with mud walls, cracks, and plastic sheeting covering the roof, which WIRED Middle East visited.
In Al Maghazi, Jawad describes five displacement sites across the camp’s western and northern areas.
Israeli bombardment has damaged sewage manhole covers in Al Maghazi, Jawad says.
The resulting openings allow rainwater to pour into sewage networks unable to accommodate the extra volume, causing wastewater to overflow.
“I consider spending money on maintaining wells or maintaining generators to operate water wells a higher priority than allocating some of that money to maintaining sewage manhole covers,” Jawad says.
